note: Review cases for the workbench (bench.html → Review cases): 300 invented communities drafted by web Claude on 2026-10-11, written blind to our lists, then given set-up answers. Set A (200) has values, and students rate the suggested approaches; set B (100) has none, and students rate the suggested values. notes and tricky are for the students; setupNotes says where a set-up choice was hard. For review only, never tuned on. Workbench only; delete before launch.

communities.name: Kemi's Reading Room

description.purpose: My little corner of Discord for people who actually finish books (or at least start them with good intentions). I post what I'm reading and my blog reviews before they go live, and we argue about endings. There's a channel for Nigerian and African lit, one for whatever romance I'm embarrassed about this week, and a monthly pick we all try to read.
description.culture: Spoilers go in spoiler tags or I will find you. Be nice about people's taste, even if it's bad.

communities.notes: About 15 people, mostly Kemi's friends from uni and a few blog readers she's met. She's the only admin and makes all the decisions; nobody has ever questioned that.

communities.name: Nguyễn Family

description.purpose: Gia đình họ Nguyễn: family news, photos, giỗ dates and Tết plans for everyone in Hà Nội and overseas.

communities.notes: 23 members across three generations in Vietnam, Germany and Australia. The eldest uncle posts the anniversary reminders and everyone defers to him; the younger cousins mostly react with stickers.

communities.name: Los Domingueros

description.purpose: Nueve amigos desde el colegio, now in our forties. Every Sunday someone hosts the asado, following the rota pinned at the top. The host buys the meat; everyone else brings wine and complaints. We also organise the yearly trip to the coast.
description.culture: We have a Constitution (capital C), written in 2009 on a napkin and transcribed by Pablo. Changes to the rota, the trip destination or whether to let in anyone's new partner go to a vote: show of hands in the chat, simple majority, Martín counts. Abstaining costs you a bottle of Malbec. Yes, we're serious. Mostly.

communities.notes: A close friend group that uses mock-formal procedures, half as a joke and half because it genuinely stops arguments. The votes are real and get respected, even when the result is silly.

communities.name: Hausgemeinschaft Kirchgasse 12

description.purpose:
This is the group for residents of Kirchgasse 12 (Stiege 1 and 2, 31 flats). We use it for things that affect the whole building: deliveries left in the hall, the laundry room schedule, who has the spare key for the bike cellar, and anything to do with the Hausverwaltung.

The group started in winter 2022, when the heating failed for eleven days and nobody at the property management answered. A few of us knocked on every door, collected signatures and phone numbers, and set up this Signal group plus a printed notice board by the mailboxes for those who don't use smartphones (Frau Hollerer in 1/4 and the Petrović family). Since then we have handled two more disputes with the Hausverwaltung, about the operating cost statement and the courtyard trees, and both times it helped that we spoke with one voice.

How we do things: Anyone can post. Important things, like a letter to the Hausverwaltung, are drafted by whoever volunteers, posted here for at least five days, and then sent if nobody objects. If someone does object, we talk it over in the courtyard on a Sunday afternoon. Thomas (2/7) and Aylin (1/2) are the admins. They keep the member list up to date when people move in or out and make sure the notice board copies of important posts are printed.

Right now we're discussing whether to formally become a Mieterbeirat (tenants' council), which some people think would give us more weight with the Hausverwaltung, while others worry it means more bureaucracy and elections nobody wants.
description.culture: Please be polite and patient. Not everyone is fluent in German, so short and clear messages help, and translations are welcome. No advertising, no politics, no forwarded chain messages. Complaints about a specific neighbour should go to that neighbour first, not in the group.

communities.notes: Mixed building of long-time older tenants, young families and students, with Turkish, Serbian, Polish and Austrian households. In practice the two admins do most of the work, and the Mieterbeirat question is starting to divide people along old-timer/newcomer lines.

communities.name: Tamale Youth Budget Hearings

description.purpose: The Tamale Metropolitan Assembly invites young people aged 15–35 to share their priorities for next year's budget. Post your ideas here, join our monthly radio call-in on Saturday mornings, or come to the open hearing at the Assembly Hall. A summary of what we hear goes to the Budget Committee, and we post their response back here.
description.culture: Respect one another. Speak about issues, not personalities, and no party campaigning. Dagbani, English and Hausa are all welcome.

communities.notes: Run by a youth desk officer at the Assembly, with an NGO partner moderating the Facebook group. Lots of engagement around jobs and streetlights, but people are sceptical anything changes, and posts often drift into party arguments that the moderator has to remove.

communities.name: Brightloom Analytics

description.purpose: 40 data people, zero managers: we pick our projects, set our own pay bands together, and nothing big happens until everyone it affects has had a chance to object.

communities.notes: A remote analytics consultancy run on consent-based decision-making with rotating client leads. It works, but slowly: the pay-band review took four months, and newer hires sometimes don't know who to ask for anything.

communities.name: Nairobi Women in Logistics

description.purpose: A network for women working in freight, warehousing, clearing and forwarding, trucking and supply chain in and around Nairobi. We share job openings, KRA and customs updates, and contacts, and we pair newer members with mentors who have been in the industry for years. Every quarter there's a breakfast meetup, usually near the ICD.
description.culture: This is a professional space but a supportive one. Ask anything; nobody will laugh at you for not knowing what a bill of lading is. Job posts must include the company name. No MLM or loan schemes, please, or you will be removed.

communities.notes: Started by three women at a clearing firm and grew to about 600 across several WhatsApp groups in one community, plus a LinkedIn page. The founders still approve every new member personally, which is becoming a bottleneck.

communities.name: Klasse 11b – Gymnasium Lindenhof

description.purpose:
This is the online space for class 11b. Assignments, materials and deadlines for all subjects are posted on Moodle by the subject teachers. Teams is used for our class chat, for remote lessons when needed, and for class council (Klassenrat) business.

Moodle: each subject has its own course. Hand in work through Moodle unless your teacher says otherwise. Late submissions are marked as late automatically; if you have a reason, message the teacher directly, not the class chat.

Teams: the General channel is for class announcements from Herr Baumann (class teacher) and the class representatives, Lea and Jonas. The Klassenrat channel is where we collect topics for our fortnightly class council meeting. Anyone can add a topic until Thursday evening. During the meeting, decisions are taken by majority vote among students. Herr Baumann has a vote too but uses his veto only on things that break school rules. There's also an off-topic channel students set up themselves; teachers can see it but don't post there.

Rules we agreed on in the first Klassenrat this year:
- No screenshots of other people's messages leaving the class.
- Phones away during lessons unless the teacher asks you to use them.
- If you're absent, it's your job to check Moodle and ask a classmate, not the teacher, for what you missed.
- Group work files go in the shared OneDrive folder with everyone's name on them.

This term we've had a problem with people posting answers to homework in the off-topic channel. The Klassenrat decided to keep the channel but appoint two students to remind people, and Herr Baumann will delete posts if it continues.
description.culture: We want a class where people help each other without doing each other's homework. Be respectful, including in the off-topic channel.

communities.notes: 24 students aged 16–17 at a Zurich gymnasium. The class council is real but the class teacher's opinion carries a lot of weight; students are torn between wanting a relaxed chat and not wanting to get the off-topic channel shut down.

communities.name: Save the Kilnwick Line

description.purpose: We're campaigning to reopen the Kilnwick to Harnby railway, closed in 1965, to passengers. Join to get updates, sign the petition, help with leafleting, or write to your MP and councillors. We now have over 4,000 supporters!
description.culture: Welcome to all our new members since the TV piece! Please read the pinned post before asking questions; most are answered there. Keep it friendly and on topic. Our committee meets monthly and will get back to you, but we are all volunteers.

communities.notes: A small committee of mostly retired rail enthusiasts, suddenly with ten times the members after regional news coverage. Newcomers want rallies and quick action; the committee wants feasibility studies and is struggling to moderate the volume.
communities.setupNotes: answered by committee; newer members might differ

communities.name: Bonsai Brasil

description.purpose: Fórum brasileiro de bonsai: cultivo, técnicas, espécies nativas, exposições e troca de mudas.

communities.notes: About 8,000 registered users, roughly 300 active. Run since 2006 by two veteran growers in São Paulo with a handful of volunteer moderators per region.

communities.name: Tessellate

description.purpose: Tessellate is a fast, safe 2D/3D computational geometry library for Rust: triangulation, boolean ops, spatial indexing. This repo and Matrix room are where we develop it. Bug reports and PRs are welcome; for larger changes please open an RFC in the rfcs/ directory first so we can discuss the design before you write the code.
description.culture: We follow the Contributor Covenant. Reviews focus on the code, not the person. Newcomers: look for issues tagged good-first-issue, and don't be shy about asking in the Matrix room.

communities.notes: About 120 contributors, but four maintainers do most reviews and hold merge rights. Decisions on RFCs are formally 'maintainer consensus', which in practice means whoever has time.

communities.name: Holy Trinity Parish Choir

description.purpose:
Welcome to the Messenger group of the Holy Trinity Parish Choir! We serve at the 9:00 a.m. Sunday Mass, Simbang Gabi, Holy Week, weddings and funerals when the family requests. This group is for practice schedules, song line-ups, announcements and prayer requests.

Practice is Wednesday 7–9 p.m. and Saturday 4–6 p.m. in the parish hall. Members are expected to attend at least one practice a week to sing at Sunday Mass. Uniforms: white on regular Sundays, maroon on feast days. Please inform the choir president, Sis. Marites, if you will be absent.

Our officers are elected every two years: president, secretary, treasurer and music director. Fr. Dodong is our spiritual adviser and has the final say on anything to do with the liturgy. The music director prepares the line-up for each Mass based on the readings; members may suggest songs to her by Wednesday.

This year we have welcomed many young members from the Youth Ministry, praise God! Some have asked to sing more contemporary praise songs and to add guitar and cajón. The officers discussed this with Fr. Dodong, and we have agreed to try one contemporary song per Mass during Ordinary Time, chosen by the music director together with a youth representative. Let us be patient with each other as we learn together.

We also raise funds for our choir through caroling every December, and we use it for our uniforms, sheet music and the choir's annual outing.
description.culture: We sing to pray, not to perform. Please be on time, keep the group for choir matters only, and avoid side comments about other members' voices. Charity first!

communities.notes: 45 members, half veterans in their 50s–60s who have sung together for decades, half newcomers from the youth ministry. It's both a liturgical ministry under the priest's authority and a music club with elected officers, and the song-choice compromise is fragile.

communities.name: Adeyemi Soil Microbiome Lab

description.purpose: Workspace for the Adeyemi Lab, Department of Microbiology. We study soil microbial communities in cassava and yam farming systems. Use #general for lab news, #equipment to book the PCR machine and incubators, #papers to share reading, and #fieldwork to plan sampling trips. Data goes in the shared drive, never on personal laptops only.
description.culture: Ask early, ask often. If you break something, say so. Lab meeting is Monday 10 a.m.; everyone presents once a month.

communities.notes: 14 people: the PI, two postdocs, five PhD students, MSc students and a technician. The PI is warm but makes all major decisions; equipment booking disputes are the main source of friction.

communities.name: Lichen Watch Cymru

description.purpose: Record lichens on trees near you and help map air quality across Wales. / Cofnodwch gennau ar goed ger eich cartref.

communities.notes: About 900 volunteers, run by a small environmental charity with one paid coordinator and a few expert verifiers who check every identification. Most volunteers never post in the mailing list.

communities.name: Kopi Talk

description.purpose: Malaysia's favourite place to lepak online since 2004. Talk about anything: makan, cars, kerja, property, football, gadgets, gossip. Yes, we moved. The old host was shutting down so we brought everyone over. Accounts and old threads are imported, but some attachments are lost, sorry.
description.culture: New forum, new mod team, same Kopi Talk. Rules are being updated; until then the old rules apply, plus: no 3R (race, religion, royalty) provocation, and no scam or loan sharks. Mods are volunteers. Report, don't fight.

communities.notes: About 60,000 accounts, maybe 5,000 really active. The original owner has stepped back after the migration and a new volunteer mod team is rewriting rules, while old members complain about everything that's changed.

communities.name: Long Shift

description.purpose:
Long Shift is a peer support server for nurses, HCAs and midwives who work nights. It was started in 2021 by two ICU nurses, one in Manchester and one in Toronto, who kept messaging each other at 4 a.m. because nobody else was awake. Now we're about 3,000 people in a lot of time zones, which means someone is always around.

What happens here:
- #3am-club: the main hangout. Vent, chat, share the absurd thing that happened on shift.
- #sleep-and-recovery: tips for sleeping during the day, managing rotating rotas, getting your body back on your days off.
- #hard-shifts: for after a death, an assault, a near-miss or just a bad night. This channel has stricter rules (see below) and trained peer listeners.
- #career: changing specialties, leaving nursing, going back to school.
- Voice rooms for 'study with me' and quiet company while you chart.

Rules (the short version):
1. No identifying patients, colleagues or employers. Ever. Change details. If in doubt, leave it out.
2. This is not a place for clinical advice. We can share experience; we can't tell you what to do with a patient.
3. In #hard-shifts, respond with support, not solutions, unless someone asks for advice. No 'at least' or 'you should have'.
4. If you are in crisis or thinking about harming yourself, please contact local emergency services or a crisis line. Pinned in every channel is a list by country. A peer listener can sit with you while you do it.
5. Respect every role. HCAs, students and agency staff are all equals here.

How it's run: we have six admins (the two founders and four people elected last year by members) and about 25 volunteer moderators and peer listeners, who complete a short training on listening skills and when to escalate. Admins meet once a month on a call. Big changes get posted in #announcements for a week of comments before they happen.

We're currently discussing whether to let in night-shift workers from other jobs (paramedics, care-home staff, security), which some members want and others feel would dilute the space.
description.culture: Kind, a bit dark-humoured, and honest. We get it. You don't have to explain why you're eating cereal at 6 p.m.

communities.notes: Feels like a well-run, warm community, but the volunteer peer listeners are stretched thin, especially after big news events. The membership question touches on identity: is this about nursing or about nights?

communities.name: Panadería Raíz

description.purpose: Somos una cooperativa de trabajadoras y trabajadores: twelve of us own and run a bakery in Colonia Doctores. This Telegram group is for the cooperativa: shift swaps, supply orders, the weekly asamblea agenda and its minutes. Customers, please follow our public channel instead.
description.culture: Una persona, un voto. Roles rotate every three months, including who deals with the accountant (nobody's favourite). We decide in the Monday asamblea after closing; if you can't come, leave your opinion in the group before. We try to disagree to people's faces, not behind their backs.

communities.notes: Formed when the previous owner retired and sold to the staff. The founding bakers hold a lot of informal authority, and the two newest members say they still don't feel like equals.

communities.name: Kuopio Ice Swimming Society

description.purpose: Avanto improves circulation, boosts mood and builds resilience: join us in the cold water of Kallavesi all winter long!

communities.notes: A registered association (ry) of about 400 members with a board, annual fees and a key system for the sauna and ice hole. None of that is in the description; the Facebook group is mostly water-temperature photos.
communities.setupNotes: filled in quickly, left at defaults

communities.name: Kurdish Students of Berlin

description.purpose: Kurdish students and young people in Berlin, from all parts of Kurdistan and all dialects. We organise Newroz, film nights and Kurmanji and Sorani conversation evenings, and we help each other with WG-hunting, Anmeldung, uni applications and visas. Instagram is for events; join the WhatsApp community for everything else.
description.culture: Everyone is welcome regardless of politics, religion, or which dialect you speak (or don't). Please keep party politics out of the group. We're here to support each other and enjoy our culture together.

communities.notes: About 250 members with an elected board of five students that changes every year. Keeping it non-political is a constant effort, and occasional heated posts lead to members leaving.

communities.name: The Slow Loaf

description.purpose:
Hello, and welcome to the oven. The Slow Loaf is my weekly newsletter about sourdough, slow food and life in a too-small kitchen in Cork. I started it in 2020, when I was baking to stay sane and everyone was asking me for my starter. It's now about 18,000 subscribers, around 5,000 of whom have joined the Discord or comment regularly.

How it works: free subscribers get the Sunday letter and can comment. Paid subscribers (the 'Proofers') also get the monthly deep-dive recipes, live bake-alongs on Discord, and the #bake-clinic channel, where you post your crumb shots and I or one of our bake-clinic volunteers will tell you what happened. The rest of the Discord, including #show-your-loaf, #starters and #off-the-bread, is open to anyone who subscribes.

I'm one person (plus my partner, who does the admin and occasionally the dishes). The Discord is moderated by four lovely Proofers who've been here since the start: Aoife, Marcus, Priya and Dee. They make day-to-day calls. If something's contentious, they bring it to me, and I make the final call, because my name's on the door.

A few rules:
- Be kind about other people's bread. Everyone's first loaf is a brick.
- No selling, including your own starters or courses, without asking the mods.
- Gluten-free and dietary questions welcome. Diet-culture talk ('carbs are poison') is not.
- Don't share paid recipes outside the community. It's how I pay the rent.

The recent bit of drama: in the spring, a member started reposting the paid recipes to a big Facebook group, and someone else defended them on the grounds that 'recipes can't be owned'. It got heated. The mods removed the poster and we wrote the last rule above. I'm still thinking about whether to make more things free.
description.culture: Cosy, nerdy about hydration percentages, a little bit sweary. Kitchen-table energy.

communities.notes: A creator-led community where the creator's word is final but the long-time volunteer mods do almost everything. The free/paid split creates quiet resentment from free members who feel second-class.

communities.name: Canopy Commons DAO

description.purpose: Canopy Commons is a community-owned DAO funding tropical reforestation and verified carbon removal. CANOPY holders propose and vote on which projects receive treasury funds via Snapshot. Anyone can join the Discord, learn about our partner projects in Borneo and Pará, and help with research and outreach.
description.culture: Fully decentralized and community-governed. Every voice matters. WAGMI 🌳

communities.notes: About 2,500 Discord members but only a few dozen ever vote. The founder holds a large share of tokens and controls the multisig, so in practice proposals that he doesn't support simply don't pass.
communities.setupNotes: answered from stated ideals, not practice

communities.name: Hiro's Train Photos

description.purpose: Hiro's server for train pics. Post what you catch.

communities.notes: Six friends from a Nagoya high school who still trade photos of trains and occasionally plan photo trips. Hiro made the server and nobody's ever needed a rule.

communities.name: Okafor Family Union

description.purpose: The official platform of the Okafor Umunna Family Union, descendants of late Pa Josiah Okafor of Nnewi, at home and in the diaspora. We use this group for meeting notices, dues reminders, welfare (weddings, burials, school fees support) and the Family August Meeting. Minutes of meetings are posted by the Secretary.
description.culture: Members are reminded that annual dues are N20,000 (diaspora: £50 or $60), payable to the Treasurer by 31st July. The Chairman's decisions on welfare requests are final after consultation with the Executive. Respect elders. No political or religious debates. Family matters must not leave this group.

communities.notes: About 140 members across Nigeria, the UK and the US. It runs like a formal association with an elected chairman, secretary, treasurer, constitution and fines for missing meetings, which is common for Igbo extended families but unusual for a family chat. The younger diaspora generation pays dues but rarely speaks.

communities.name: The Halfway House

description.purpose:
Named after 43 Halfway Road, Sheffield, 2014–2017, the worst and best house any of us ever lived in. Eleven of us lived there at various points (it was a six-bed, don't ask). This server is how we stay in touch now that we're scattered across Leeds, London, Glasgow, Berlin and, for some reason, Perth.

What's here: #the-kitchen for general chat; #mouldwatch for photos of our current flats; #plans for the annual reunion weekend; #games for when we do Jackbox on a Friday. Plus a voice channel nobody uses except Dan, who sits in it alone like a lighthouse keeper.

How things work: there aren't really rules. Sam set it up and is technically the admin, but everyone has the same permissions because Sam got bored of being asked. Reunion location and dates are picked by whoever volunteers to organise that year, with a poll if there's a clash. Money for shared stuff goes through a Splitwise.

The recent thing: Jess's wedding invite went out and didn't include Tom, and Tom found out from the reunion channel. It turned into a long, painful thread. Some people think wedding stuff shouldn't be discussed in the server at all; others think it's daft to pretend. For now, we've agreed to keep wedding talk to DMs and move on, and the reunion is going ahead in October.
description.culture: Affectionately rude. Nothing is sacred except the memory of the 2016 kitchen fire.

communities.notes: A tight, informal group with no structure until something goes wrong. The wedding fallout exposed that nobody actually has the authority to set norms, and two members have gone quiet since.

communities.name: Vecinos Barrio Yungay

description.purpose: Grupo de vecinos y vecinas del Barrio Yungay. Avisos de seguridad, mascotas perdidas, cortes de agua y luz, ferias, actividades culturales, y todo lo relacionado con la protección de nuestro barrio patrimonial. Somos más de 250 vecinos, de Matucana a Brasil.
description.culture: Respeto ante todo. Nada de política partidista, ventas solo los viernes, y nada de discriminación hacia los vecinos migrantes. Si ves algo urgente, llama primero a Carabineros y después avisa aquí.

communities.notes: Run by three admins from the local junta de vecinos. Security posts dominate, and there's recurring tension over posts that blame immigrant neighbours, which the admins remove but not always quickly.

communities.name: Have Your Say: Ōtaki Wastewater

description.purpose: Tell us what you think about the three options for upgrading Ōtaki's wastewater treatment plant: land disposal, upgraded river discharge, or a hybrid.

communities.notes: A district council consultation page with a comment form and a moderated discussion board. The description says nothing about who reads submissions or how the decision gets made; local iwi are consulted separately, and that's where most of the real influence sits.

communities.name: Kestrel Freight Dispatch

description.purpose: Teams channel for the Rotterdam depot dispatch team. Shift handovers go in the Handover thread every morning and evening: open loads, delays, driver issues, anything the next shift needs. Use the Swaps tab for shift swaps (team lead approves). Urgent driver issues: phone, not chat.
description.culture: Keep it short and clear, in English or Dutch. If you dropped something, flag it, so we don't find out from the customer.

communities.notes: 35 dispatchers across three shifts and two team leads. Night shift has its own informal WhatsApp where the real complaints happen, and management doesn't know it exists.

communities.name: Court Interpreters Exchange

description.purpose:
The Court Interpreters Exchange (CIX) is a mailing list for interpreters working in courts, tribunals and legal settings across Canada, in any language pair, including ASL and LSQ. It was started in 1998 by a small group of Toronto-based Spanish and Portuguese interpreters, and now has about 1,200 subscribers.

What the list is for:
- Terminology questions ('How do you render "recognizance" in Tagalog?')
- Sharing glossaries and resources
- Discussing professional practice: positioning, conflicts of interest, what to do when a lawyer asks you to summarise
- News about accreditation, ministry policies and fee schedules

What the list is not for: job postings from agencies (there's a separate announcements list), personal disputes, or anything that could identify a case, a party or a witness.

Moderation: the list is moderated by a volunteer team of three, currently Marie-Claude (Montréal), Harjit (Surrey) and Olumide (Ottawa). New members' first three posts are held for review. Members who break confidentiality are removed without warning. Other problems get a private warning first.

A few long-standing norms:
- Use a clear subject line with the language pair in brackets, e.g. [ES-EN] or [ALL].
- Reply to the list only if your answer helps everyone; otherwise reply privately.
- Disagree about the term, not the interpreter.
- Fee discussions are allowed in general terms, but no coordinating rates (we've had legal advice on this).

Over the last two years the fee debate has become the main topic, as several provinces have frozen rates and agencies have taken a bigger cut. Some members want the list to take positions or organise; others want it to stay a purely professional exchange. The moderators have proposed a separate, opt-in advocacy list, and comments are open until the end of the month.
description.culture: Collegial, precise, occasionally pedantic (it's the job). Many of us work alone, so this list is our break room.

communities.notes: A quiet, old-fashioned list with very high trust, where confidentiality is sacred. The fee question is splitting it between those who see it as a professional forum and those who want something closer to a union.

communities.name: Medielinja 2026 – Fjordvik Folkehøgskole

description.purpose: Discord for Medielinja (the media line) at Fjordvik folk high school, 2025–26. Film, photo and podcast projects, equipment booking, feedback on each other's work, and planning our study trip to Lisbon.
description.culture: No grades, no exams; we're here to make stuff and learn from each other. We set our own rules: at the start of the year we wrote them together in #allmøte, and anyone can propose a change there. A change is adopted if a majority of the line votes for it at the weekly allmøte on Monday. Kari (our teacher) has one vote like everyone else, though she can stop things that break school or Norwegian law. So far we've voted on equipment rules, quiet hours in the edit suite and where to go on the trip.

communities.notes: 30 students aged 19–24 living at the school. The student democracy is real but strong personalities dominate the votes, and Kari quietly steers more than the rules suggest.

communities.name: Bike Lanes for Kraków

description.purpose: Walczymy o bezpieczne, chronione drogi rowerowe w Krakowie. We fight for safe, protected bike lanes in Kraków.

communities.notes: About 7,000 members, run by a small registered association that writes the formal submissions to the city. The Facebook group is mostly near-miss videos and arguments with drivers.

communities.name: Fen Knitters

description.purpose: Knitters, crocheters and spinners from around Ely, March and the Fens. We chat patterns and projects here, swap and destash yarn, and meet on the second Tuesday of the month at the Lamb in Ely, 7pm till the landlord kicks us out.
description.culture: All crafts, all levels, all speeds. Frogging encouraged. Don't ask anyone when the jumper will be finished.

communities.notes: About 300 members on Ravelry, 15–20 who come to the pub. Run by two friends who share the group admin; everything is very relaxed except the yearly charity blanket drive, which is surprisingly well organised.

communities.name: OpenHerbaria

description.purpose:
OpenHerbaria is a community-maintained, openly licensed dataset of digitised herbarium specimen records, with a wiki for documentation and transcription guidelines. Volunteers and botanists transcribe labels from specimen images, georeference collection localities and fix taxonomy so the records can be used for research on plant distributions and climate change.

We began in March of this year as a fork of the Herbarium Commons project. Most of our core contributors spent years in Herbarium Commons, and the full dataset up to February has been carried over under its CC0 dedication. We split because of disagreements over governance: the old project's steering board decided, without consulting contributors, to accept funding from a data company and to delay public releases by twelve months. We respect the people still working there and we're happy to share fixes in both directions.

How OpenHerbaria works:
- All records and the wiki are CC0. They stay CC0. This can't be changed by any vote.
- Anyone can transcribe. Edits by new contributors are reviewed by an experienced editor before they're published.
- Taxonomic decisions follow the published backbone listed on the wiki. Disagreements go to the Taxonomy talk page; if unresolved after two weeks, the taxonomy working group decides.
- We have an interim coordinating group of five people, chosen at the founding call. Their job is to run the infrastructure and draft a governance charter within six months. The draft charter is on the wiki for comments.
- Releases are quarterly, with no embargo.

One current issue: about 40,000 records were imported from a regional herbarium that had a partnership with the old project, and the herbarium has asked whether we have permission to use their images. We believe the transcriptions are fine but are checking the image licences and may need to remove them.
description.culture: Open by default and careful with the data. We'd rather move slowly and get the record right. Credit everyone who did the work, especially volunteers.

communities.notes: About 400 contributors, with a few hundred very active. Morale is high but there's bitterness toward the parent project, and the 'interim' group may become permanent if the charter stalls.

communities.name: Masjid Al-Noor Sisters' Circle

description.purpose: Assalamu alaikum sisters! This group is for the sisters of Masjid Al-Noor. Here you'll find our Thursday halaqah times, Qur'an class schedule, Ramadan iftar rota, and news about the sisters' section. Please also share du'a requests and support each other.
description.culture: Please keep the group for beneficial reminders and masjid matters. No forwards without checking authenticity, no selling, no backbiting. Be gentle with each other. This is a safe space for all sisters, new Muslims especially.

communities.notes: About 80 women of mostly Gujarati and Somali heritage, with a few converts. Two aunties run it with the masjid committee's blessing; the younger sisters run their own separate chat for socials.

communities.name: Ice Core Group

description.purpose: Internal chat, ice core team, IGE Grenoble.

communities.notes: About 20 people: researchers, engineers, PhD students and a cold-room technician. Very hierarchical in planning field campaigns, informal in the chat, with French and English mixed.

communities.name: Delhi Clean Air Sensors

description.purpose: We are Delhi residents who host low-cost PM2.5 sensors on our balconies and rooftops, building a hyperlocal air quality map the government doesn't provide. Our data is public on our dashboard. We also use it to push for action: RTI requests, letters to the DPCC, and showing up at hearings with evidence.
description.culture: Data first. Don't exaggerate, and don't post rumours about readings; check the dashboard. Sensor hosts get priority for help with setup. Everyone is welcome at protests, but no one has to come.

communities.notes: About 400 members, half sensor hosts, half activists who joined for campaigns. The technical volunteers worry campaigning undermines the data's credibility; the campaigners think data without action is pointless.
communities.setupNotes: could be movement; campaigners would add direct_action

communities.name: moss.town

description.purpose:
moss.town is a general-interest Mastodon server for people who want a slower, kinder corner of the fediverse. We started in late 2022, during the first big wave of people leaving the bird site. Four friends who had been running a tiny server for themselves suddenly had 6,000 sign-ups in a week. We're now around 18,000 accounts, about 4,000 active monthly.

What we're about: posting about your garden, your cat, your bad day, your research, your knitting, your city. No particular topic. We like long posts, alt text and content warnings, and we like people who use them.

How it runs:
- moss.town is funded entirely by donations through Open Collective; the costs and spending are public. We have no ads and never will.
- We have three admins (two of the founders plus a sysadmin who joined in 2023) and a moderation team of 11 volunteers in different time zones.
- Moderation decisions are logged (anonymised) in a public moderation log, updated monthly.
- Sign-ups are open with a short application ('Why do you want to join?'), which is mostly a spam filter.

Our rules, in short:
1. No racism, sexism, homophobia, transphobia, ableism, or other bigotry.
2. Use content warnings for politics, violence, food and bodies, and anything distressing. Alt text on images, please.
3. No harassment, dogpiling or quote-dunking on people from other servers.
4. No commercial spam. Small creators sharing their work occasionally is fine.
5. Don't post anything illegal in Germany (where our server is).

Federation: we block servers that host harassment or hate. Our blocklist is public, with reasons. Recently, members argued for weeks about whether to block a large new server run by a big tech company. Some said we should block preemptively to protect the community; others said that would cut people off from friends. In the end, the admins ran a members' poll; 58% voted to limit (not fully block) the server, and that's what we did. Some members left over it, both ways.
description.culture: Slow, cosy, a bit nerdy. Assume good faith, then use the report button.

communities.notes: Formally donation-funded and admin-run, with an informal tradition of consulting members on big decisions. The defederation poll set a precedent the admins aren't sure they want to repeat, because it brought in a lot of anger.

communities.name: Grief After Pets

description.purpose: A place for anyone grieving the loss of a beloved animal companion: dogs, cats, horses, rabbits, birds, reptiles, all of them. Share their story and their photos, talk about the hard days, the guilt about euthanasia, the empty spot on the sofa. Whether it was yesterday or ten years ago, your grief is welcome here.
description.culture: No judging anyone's decisions or how long they grieve. No 'just get another one'. No selling (including pet portraits and urns). Memorial posts every Sunday 🌈

communities.notes: About 9,000 members, very active, run by one founder and four volunteer admins who approve every post. Mostly US and UK. Emotional and supportive, but admins quietly burn out from the volume of heavy posts.

communities.name: Lavoro Comune

description.purpose: Olio extravergine di oliva Coratina, Ogliarola e Peranzana, dalla Puglia: bottiglie, latte da 3 e 5 litri.

communities.notes: Actually an agricultural co-op of about 60 grower families with a general assembly, an elected board and a shared press. The email list is where members argue about pricing and harvest quotas, but the description is just the product list from their shop page.

communities.name: Accra Chess Club

description.purpose: Accra's home for chess. Blitz every Saturday at 3pm (venue in the pinned message), monthly rapid tournaments, junior coaching on Sunday mornings, and a Lichess club for online arenas during the week. FIDE-rated or total beginner, come and play.
description.culture: Touch-move applies, even in casual games 😄. Respect your opponent, shake hands, and no trash talk aimed at juniors.

communities.notes: About 150 members, run by a small committee who collect monthly dues for venue hire. A few strong players dominate decisions about tournaments, and there's ongoing debate about how much of the budget goes to juniors.

communities.name: Rainbow Majlis

description.purpose:
Rainbow Majlis is a private Discord server for LGBTQ+ Arabs, and people of Arab heritage, living in the UK. A majlis is a sitting room where people gather, talk and look after each other, and that's what we want this to be.

We have channels for general chat, coming out (or not coming out) to family, faith and spirituality, immigration and asylum questions, dating, food, music, and Arabic language practice in different dialects. We hold online events monthly and small in-person meetups in London, Manchester and Birmingham.

Privacy and joining:
Many of us are not out, have family who could be at risk, or are going through the asylum system. Your safety comes first. To join, you'll have a short voice or video call with one of our verification team. We'll never ask for your real name or ID. We just want to be sure you're part of the community and not someone hostile.

Rules:
1. What's said in the majlis stays in the majlis. No screenshots, no sharing anyone's identity, photos or story outside the server. Breaking this means a permanent ban.
2. Use a nickname. You don't have to show your face.
3. Respect all faiths and none. Debating religion is fine; mocking someone's faith or their lack of it isn't.
4. No outing anyone, even jokingly.
5. No dating or hookup requests in public channels; use the opt-in #dating channel.

The server is run by five admins and a verification team of eight. Admins are chosen by the existing admin team, with input from members.

What happened in January: screenshots from #faith-and-spirituality appeared on an account on another platform, with usernames visible. Nobody's real identity was exposed, but several members were frightened and left. We have since removed the person responsible, tightened verification, turned off image downloads where we can, and created a separate high-privacy area for members who need extra protection. We know trust takes time to rebuild.
description.culture: Warm like a family dinner, minus the questions about when you're getting married. Mixed Arabic and English welcome, yalla.

communities.notes: About 1,500 members, very close-knit, with safety concerns that shape every rule. After the leak, the vetting is strict enough that some members feel the community has become cliquish and slow to welcome newcomers.

communities.name: Foxglove & Frets

description.purpose: Home of the Foxglove & Frets community: folk, fingerstyle and cosy music streams. While Wren is taking time away, the server stays open. Our mod team is running the weekly open-mic stream, the song-of-the-week, and the learning channels. Post your covers, ask about tunings, and hang out.
description.culture: Wren asked us to keep this place gentle and welcoming while she's gone, and we will. Please don't speculate about her health or when she's back; she'll tell us when she's ready. Mod decisions are made by the mod team together.

communities.notes: About 12,000 Discord members. The streamer left for health reasons four months ago with no return date, and five mods now run everything, including a community stream on the mod account. Some members treat the mods as stand-ins, others think they've overstepped.
communities.setupNotes: filled in by a mod during the transition

communities.name: Pixelpot DAO

description.purpose: Pixel artists pooling funds and minting together. Hold a Pot, vote on drops. gm 👾

communities.notes: About 800 Discord members left from a bigger 2022 launch; maybe 30 are active. A core of artists makes decisions in a private channel, and token votes are mostly rubber stamps.

communities.name: Tomás's Garden Diary

description.purpose: My diary from the huerto in Murcia. I post what's growing, what died, what I'm cooking with it and what I'm thinking about while I weed. Just me talking to you like we're leaning on the fence. You can react and answer the polls.
description.culture: This is my little space, so I'll be honest: I can't read every message, but I read a lot of them. Be kind to each other in the replies.

communities.notes: Written like an intimate personal diary, but it's an Instagram broadcast channel with about 20,000 followers and brand deals. Followers can only react and vote in polls, so it's a one-to-many 'community' that feels personal.

communities.name: Syskonen Lindqvist

description.purpose:
This is our chat for the eight of us, mostly about Mamma now. Since Pappa died last year and Mamma's memory got worse, we've been using this to coordinate who visits, who takes her to the doctor, and money.

The practical stuff we agreed on at Christmas:
- Visits: there's a shared calendar (link pinned). Mamma should have a visitor at least four days a week. Those of us in Umeå (Karin, Erik, Lotta) do most weekday visits. The rest of us do weekends when we can and pay towards the cost of the home help instead.
- Money: Erik has power of attorney and manages Mamma's account. He posts a summary every month. Big expenses (anything over 5,000 kr) we discuss here first.
- Medical: Karin goes to the appointments and writes up what the doctor said here, so nobody hears it third-hand.
- The house: no decisions about selling until we've all met in person. That's the summer.

What's hard: Lotta feels she's doing far more than her share and said so in March, and it got tense. Johan and Anna live abroad and feel guilty and left out of decisions. We've started a monthly video call so it's not all happening in text, which helps.
description.culture: Let's remember we're all doing our best and we all love her. Say things in the call if they're too big for text. No sarcasm in here, please (Per).

communities.notes: Eight adult siblings aged 38–58 across Sweden, Norway and the US. There's no formal leader, but Erik's legal role and Karin's medical role give them more say than the others, which is part of the tension.

communities.name: Phở Fridays

description.purpose: Every Friday, 7pm, phở somewhere in Melbourne. Whoever's turn it is picks the place and posts it by Wednesday. Footscray and Richmond are default but we're open to adventure (within reason, Ben).
description.culture: If you're not coming, say so by Thursday, so we can book the right table. Broth critiques are mandatory.

communities.notes: Seven friends, most from a former workplace. Turn order is kept in a pinned note that nobody updates, so whoever remembers ends up picking.

communities.name: Sector 7 Allotment Neighbours

description.purpose: Residents of Sector 7 who garden in the community plots behind the park: water timings, seed swaps, monkey alerts, and anything about the colony.

communities.notes: Started as a gardening group but became the de facto residents' chat for the sector, so plot-sharing and RWA disputes mix uneasily in one place. About 60 members; the oldest gardener is unofficially in charge.

communities.name: Mesa de Movilidad Bogotá

description.purpose: Espacio de participación ciudadana de la Secretaría de Movilidad. Aquí puedes opinar sobre proyectos de ciclorrutas, TransMilenio, peatonalización y seguridad vial en tu localidad. Cada mes publicamos un tema para discusión y, al final del periodo, un informe con lo que se dijo y cómo se tuvo en cuenta.
description.culture: Participa con respeto. Se eliminarán insultos, mensajes políticos de campaña y publicidad. Los funcionarios responden los martes y jueves.

communities.notes: About 1,500 registered participants, but around 50 people post most comments, including several organised cycling and taxi groups. Officials do reply, but residents often doubt that the reports change any decisions.

communities.name: Tidewater Clinic Front Desk

description.purpose:
Group chat for front desk and scheduling staff at Tidewater Family Clinic. Use it for:
- Shift swaps (post the swap, get the other person to confirm, then tell Denise)
- Day-of coverage when someone calls out
- Quick heads-ups ("phones are down," "Dr. Patel running 40 min behind")

Do NOT put patient names, birthdays, or anything identifying in this chat. Use the EHR messaging for anything about a patient. This is a HIPAA thing, not a Denise thing.

Coverage rules: if you call out, you text Denise AND post here. Whoever picks up your shift gets first pick on the next holiday swap. Nobody works more than three late shifts in a row.

After what happened in August: we know the week Maria was out was rough, and the fight in here about who 'always' covers didn't help anyone. Denise has now set up a coverage list that rotates, posted every Monday. If it's your turn and you really can't, it's on you to find someone. Venting is fine, but take it out of this chat or talk to Denise directly.
description.culture: We're a small team and we have each other's backs. Keep it professional enough that you'd be fine with Denise reading it, because she does.

communities.notes: Nine receptionists and schedulers at a small US clinic, managed by an office manager who reads everything. The August blow-up left lasting resentment between the full-timers and two part-timers who rarely cover.

communities.name: Indie Translators Guild

description.purpose: A Discord for freelance translators and interpreters: rates talk, bad-client warnings, CAT tool help, AI and machine translation post-editing discussion, and coworking voice channels. Right now we're also discussing whether the Guild should become a formal union or association; see #the-big-question and vote by the 30th.
description.culture: Freelancers helping freelancers. Name and shame bad clients only with evidence. No agencies recruiting here. However the vote goes, we stay friends (please).

communities.notes: About 2,000 members globally, started as a casual chat with no formal leaders. The union question means drafting statutes, dues and elections, and it has already split people over whether non-EU members could join and who would represent them.

communities.name: STAT 101 – Estadística I

description.purpose: Foro del curso Estadística I, semestre 2026-1. Dudas sobre talleres, parciales y el proyecto final.

communities.notes: About 180 students in three sections with one professor and two TAs. The official Moodle forum is nearly silent; the real discussion happens in student WhatsApp groups that staff aren't in.

communities.name: Right to Repair Ireland

description.purpose: We campaign for your right to fix the things you own, from phones and laptops to tractors and washing machines. We write submissions to Government and EU consultations, support repair cafés around the country, and keep members up to date on the new EU repair rules and how they're being brought into Irish law.
description.culture: Anyone who cares about repair is welcome: tinkerers, farmers, environmentalists, small repair shops. Keep it constructive. We're for repair, not against any one company. Our steering group meets online on the first Monday of the month and minutes go to the list.

communities.notes: About 900 people across the mailing list and Mastodon, with a steering group of six volunteers. Some long-time members are frustrated that a single person writes nearly every policy submission.

communities.name: Mechanical Pencil Collectors

description.purpose:
MPC is a forum for collectors and users of mechanical pencils: vintage, Japanese, drafting, limited editions, everyday carry. We have sub-forums for identification, restoration, reviews, news and a buy/sell/trade marketplace. Since 2009.

READ BEFORE POSTING. These rules are enforced and we will not apologise for that.

1. Post formats. Identification requests must use the ID template: clear photos of the clip, the barrel imprint and the tip, plus lead size. Reviews must include lead size, weight, price paid and how long you've used it. Posts that don't follow the template will be locked with a link to this page.

2. Search first. 'What's the best pencil for school' has been answered 400 times. Duplicate threads get merged or locked.

3. Marketplace. You need 50 posts and 3 months of membership to sell. Every listing needs a photo with a handwritten note showing your username and the date. Prices must be stated; 'make an offer' is not allowed. All sales get a feedback entry. Members with negative feedback lose market access pending review.

4. Fakes. Do not sell or knowingly trade counterfeits. Suspected counterfeits get moved to the Authentication sub-forum where our three authenticators will rule. Their decision is final.

5. Conduct. Three strikes. One for off-topic or format violations after a warning, one for rudeness, one for anything else the moderators decide. Three strikes in a year is a permanent ban. Market fraud is an instant ban, and we share details with other collector forums.

6. No arguing with moderators in public threads. Use the appeals sub-forum.

Why so strict? Because in 2015 the market was overrun by scammers and the ID section was useless. Since then this has been the most reliable source of information on the hobby anywhere, and the regulars like it that way.

The forum is owned by its founder, and run day to day by seven moderators he appoints.
description.culture: Precise and helpful. We are friendly to people who make an effort. Lurk a bit before you post.

communities.notes: About 5,000 members and very high-quality information. Newcomers often find the strictness hostile for a hobby about stationery, and the authenticators have enormous informal power over what collectors' pencils are worth.

communities.name: Kitab Sabz

description.purpose: Kitab Sabz ('green book') is a volunteer library of public-domain Persian literature, history and poetry. We scan, transcribe and proofread classic works and publish them free as ebooks and web pages. Anyone can claim a page to proofread; finished books go through two rounds of checking before release.
description.culture: Accuracy and patience. Keep spelling exactly as in the source, even if it looks wrong to you, and note doubts on the talk page instead of 'fixing' them. No political debates; we publish texts, not opinions.

communities.notes: About 300 editors in Iran, Afghanistan, Tajikistan and the diaspora. A small group of senior editors approve releases, and decisions about which books count as 'political' cause occasional quiet fights.

communities.name: Leeds Zen Sitting Group

description.purpose: Weekly zazen on Wednesday evenings in Headingley. Newcomers welcome; instruction at 7pm.

communities.notes: About 40 on the list and a dozen who sit each week, led by a lay teacher authorised by a Soto Zen sangha in the US. Decisions about the group are made by the teacher and two longtime members.

communities.name: The Lumen Collective

description.purpose: We're a group of independent researchers (mostly ex-academics) working on public health, education and labour research. We do commissioned studies for NGOs, unions and local governments, and some unfunded projects we care about. Lumen is legally a worker co-op: income from projects goes into a shared pool, and everyone is paid the same day rate.
description.culture: Rigour without the academic ego. We review each other's work honestly. New projects are taken on only if two members want to lead them and nobody blocks. We meet monthly on a video call to decide what to take on and how to split the pool.

communities.notes: About 25 members across Europe and Latin America on Zulip. Functions as a research lab with peer review and methods discussions, and also as a business with income sharing, so scholarly disagreements turn into money disagreements fast.

communities.name: Galaxy Sorters

description.purpose:
Galaxy Sorters is a citizen science project where you help astronomers understand how galaxies form and change by classifying images from sky surveys. Is it smooth or does it have features? A bar? Spiral arms? How many? Each image is classified by many volunteers, and combining your answers produces data astronomers use in real research, including more than 30 published papers.

You don't need any experience. The tutorial takes five minutes, and you can classify as many or as few galaxies as you like.

The Talk forum is where volunteers and the science team chat. You can tag interesting objects (#merger, #ring, #weird), ask questions about what you're seeing, and discuss results. Some of our most important discoveries, like the 'green pea' style compact galaxies in our early data, were first noticed by volunteers on Talk.

The science team (astronomers at universities in the UK, US and Australia) posts updates, explains new results, and occasionally asks for volunteer help with special projects. Two volunteer moderators and a project manager look after Talk.

Forum guidelines:
- Be respectful and patient. Everyone was new once.
- Keep discussion about the project, galaxies and astronomy.
- Don't post classifications for others to copy. Independent answers are what make the data useful.
- Credit: volunteers who make a significant discovery will be acknowledged in any resulting paper.

A note from the science team: some volunteers have raised concerns that the credit guideline is too vague, after a paper on ring galaxies acknowledged 'Galaxy Sorters volunteers' collectively but didn't name the two people who spent months compiling the list. They're right that we could have done better. We've opened a thread to work out, together, a clearer policy on when and how individual volunteers will be named, and how volunteers can be involved in papers that come from their work.
description.culture: Curious, welcoming, a bit awestruck. There are no stupid questions about the universe.

communities.notes: About 30,000 volunteers, most of whom classify silently; a few hundred are very active on Talk. Power sits firmly with the science team, but the credit dispute has made the 'superusers' push for more of a voice.

communities.name: Olá Lisboa

description.purpose: The biggest Portuguese-speaking hangout server. Gaming, football, music, memes, study rooms, regional channels from Minho to the Algarve and the islands, plus channels for Brazilians, Angolans, Cape Verdeans and the diaspora. Events every weekend: game nights, karaoke, quizzes.
description.culture: Have fun and respect people. No racism or xenophobia; Brazilians and Portuguese, behave 😅. No football fights outside #futebol. Mods are volunteers, open a ticket if you have a problem.

communities.notes: About 25,000 members, mostly teens and twenty-somethings. Run by an owner and a large staff with a ranked hierarchy (admins, mods, helpers) and a recruitment process. Friction between European and Brazilian Portuguese speakers flares up regularly.

communities.name: Sober Curious Dads

description.purpose: Dads cutting back or quitting the booze, roasting each other through it. Daily check-in at 9pm.

communities.notes: About 200 UK fathers. The banter is relentless and that's the point; men who'd never join a traditional support group stick around. The two founders step in quickly when someone posts about a genuine crisis, but newcomers can find the tone off-putting.

communities.name: Ubuntu Housing Co-op

description.purpose: This group is for members of Ubuntu Housing Co-operative, 60 households in Cato Manor. We use it for maintenance requests, meeting notices, levy reminders, and news from the board. Our general meeting is on the last Sunday of the month at the community hall. Every household has one vote.
description.culture: We built this together and we look after it together. Pay your levy on time so everyone's house stays fixed. Raise problems with your block representative before posting complaints here. Respect our elders and the board, but hold them accountable too.

communities.notes: Formed in the 1990s with government housing support. The board is elected every two years, but the same families have held it for a decade, and arrears from a few households have caused bitter arguments.

communities.name: Dunedin Tramping Club

description.purpose:
The Dunedin Tramping Club has been getting people into the hills of Otago since 1923. We run day trips and weekend trips almost every week of the year, from easy walks on the Peninsula to hard multi-day trips in Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Park. We also own two huts, run a gear library, and hold club nights with talks and slideshows on the second Thursday of the month.

How trips work:
- Trips are listed on the website and the mailing list with a grade: Easy, Moderate, Fit, or Hard. Read the grade descriptions. If you're new, start with Easy or Moderate.
- Every trip has a leader. Contact them to sign up, at least by the Wednesday before. The leader can decline anyone they think isn't ready for that trip; please don't take it personally.
- Leaders have done our leader training (navigation, river crossing, first aid, decision-making). New leaders co-lead with an experienced one first.
- Intentions are always left with a trip contact, and every party carries a PLB.

Huts: members book through the hut warden. Non-members can use them when they're not booked, for a fee.

Membership: annual subscriptions are due on 1 April. Members get cheaper trip fees, hut use, gear library access and a vote at the AGM.

The club is run by a committee elected at the AGM: president, secretary, treasurer, trip convener, hut warden, gear officer, and three general members. Committee meetings are monthly and open to members.

At the moment the committee is reviewing our grading system after two incidents last winter in which newer members ended up on trips harder than they expected. A draft revised grading, with clearer fitness and experience requirements, is on the website, and feedback is open until the AGM.
description.culture: Friendly, safe and unpretentious. We want everyone to get home happy and tired, and we'd rather turn back than push on.

communities.notes: About 600 members across generations, with a strong safety culture and traditional committee structure. Older members prize leader discretion; younger members find it opaque and want objective criteria, which is what the grading review is really about.

communities.name: Saturday Gujarati School Parents

description.purpose: Group for parents of children at the Saturday Gujarati classes at the community centre in Scarborough. Teachers post homework and class updates, and the committee posts news about Navratri, the Diwali show, and fees. Please also use it to arrange carpools.
description.culture: Please keep messages relevant to the school and our community events. Gujarati or English are both fine. Fee issues should go privately to the treasurer. Thank you to all the volunteer teachers!

communities.notes: About 120 parents. It's half a class group and half a cultural association: the committee that runs the school also runs the community events, and parents who want stricter academic standards clash with those who mainly want their kids to have fun and keep the culture.

communities.name: Two Aunties Podcast Listeners

description.purpose: Fan group for Two Aunties, the podcast where two Singaporean aunties talk about everything you're too paiseh to ask.
description.culture: Steady lah. Be nice.

communities.notes: About 3,000 members. The hosts aren't admins; a superfan runs it, and the hosts occasionally drop in, which makes everyone very excited.

communities.name: Gridshare DAO

description.purpose: Gridshare lets neighbours in Valencia co-own solar installations on schools and warehouses. Each GRID token represents a share of an installation and its energy savings. Token holders vote on Discourse and Snapshot on new sites, maintenance budgets and how surplus income is used, for example lowering bills for families in energy poverty.
description.culture: We're a community energy project first and a crypto project second. Explain things simply; many members have never used a wallet. Proposals need a week of discussion before going to a vote.

communities.notes: About 400 participants, many of them older residents who were helped to set up wallets. A small legal foundation actually owns the panels, so token votes are legally advisory, though the foundation has so far followed every one.

communities.name: Inês's Studio Notes

description.purpose:
Hi! I'm Inês, an illustrator in Porto. This server is my studio with the door open. I share works in progress, sketchbook pages, process videos, and the thinking behind my picture-book work. It's also where students from my online illustration course and my patrons hang out.

Channels:
- #studio-window: what I'm working on, usually daily.
- #your-work: share your own drawings. Feedback only if you ask for it.
- #crit-corner: for structured critique. Post with what you want feedback on (composition? colour? character?). Give one critique for every one you get.
- #course-room: for current and past students of my course. I answer questions here on Tuesdays and Fridays.
- #patrons-only: monthly sketchbook scans, early looks, and a monthly video call.
- #free-chat: anything else, including cat photos.

Rules:
1. Critique the drawing, not the person. 'The eye isn't reading because the value contrast is low' is good. 'This is bad' is not.
2. No AI-generated images. This is a space for people learning to draw, and many of us have had our work scraped.
3. Don't repost my work or other people's outside the server without permission.
4. Self-promotion is fine in #your-work, once a week.

It's my server and I make the decisions, but I've asked two longtime students, Bea and Rui, to help moderate, and I trust their judgment.

Right now I'm thinking about whether to keep the course room open to past students forever. It's getting busy and new students say it's intimidating.
description.culture: Gentle and honest, like a good art school but without the pretension. Everyone here is learning, me included.

communities.notes: About 70 people: students, patrons and illustrator friends. It's very much Inês's personal space, but money (patrons, course fees) shapes who gets what access, and two student moderators carry more weight than their title suggests.

communities.name: Mbeki-Dube Cousins

description.purpose: The cousins' chat. Birthdays, babies, graduations, memes, and who's bringing what to Gogo's for Christmas. Also where we sort out contributions when there's a funeral or umembeso.
description.culture: Aunties are not allowed in here, that's the whole point 😂. Be kind, no politics, and if there's family drama, take it to DMs.

communities.notes: About 35 cousins in Johannesburg, Durban and London. The eldest cousin acts as unofficial treasurer for family contributions, and that arrangement is never discussed openly.

communities.name: Dead Poets Society (We're Not Dead)

description.purpose: College gang, now reading one book a month and pretending to have opinions about it.

communities.notes: Eight friends from a Chennai college who started reading together during lockdown. Half want a real book club with a schedule and discussion questions; the other half just want the group chat and the occasional dinner.

communities.name: Hillcrest Road Snow Squad

description.purpose: Neighbours on Hillcrest and the side streets who help clear driveways and walkways for seniors and anyone who can't shovel after a big snowfall. When snow is forecast, we post a sign-up. If you need help, message Linda or post here.
description.culture: No obligation; help when you can. It's neighbours being neighbourly. Hot chocolate at #14 after big storms.

communities.notes: About 60 households on a neighbourhood app group. Linda keeps the list of who needs help and quietly assigns people, which works until she's away.

communities.name: Ward 14 Residents' Association

description.purpose:
This is the official WhatsApp group of the Ward 14 Residents' Association (registered under the Societies Registration Act), covering 23 housing societies and the bungalows on the old Paud Road stretch. About 800 members. We represent residents to the Municipal Corporation, the ward office and our corporator on water supply, roads, garbage collection, encroachments and tree cutting.

The association was formed in 2011, when water tanker supply to the area kept failing. Since then we've got the main water line upgraded, three illegal hoardings removed, and a weekly dry-waste collection started.

How we work:
- Each housing society nominates one representative to the general body. The general body elects a managing committee of nine (president, two vice-presidents, secretary, treasurer and four members) every two years.
- The managing committee meets on the first Sunday of every month at the Ganesh temple hall. Meetings are open to all residents.
- Complaints: please first raise with your society representative. If it's ward-level, the representative will bring it to the committee. You can also raise it directly in this group, but give the location and a photo.
- Annual membership: Rs 500 per household, collected through societies.

Group rules: only admins post forwards. No political party publicity. No buying/selling (use the separate classifieds group). Messages in Marathi, Hindi or English.

Current issue: the builder of the new tower on Survey No. 47 has started cutting trees on the edge of the plot without the Tree Authority's permission. The committee has filed a complaint and is preparing a petition, but some members want us to go to court, which would mean raising funds. We'll be discussing this at a special general meeting on the 18th. Please attend or send your society representative with your views.
description.culture: We are a non-political, non-religious body. We can disagree, but let's keep it civil, and let's not abuse officials in this group, even when they deserve it.

communities.notes: Mostly older, middle-class homeowners; tenants and the nearby informal settlement aren't represented at all. The committee is effective with officials partly because some members have political connections, which sits awkwardly with the 'non-political' claim.

communities.name: Northbeam Games QA

description.purpose: Slack for Northbeam QA: test plans, bug triage, build notes and who's on which branch. As of this month we're part of Ravelstone Interactive, so some of this will move to their tools. We'll post updates here as we learn more.
description.culture: We've always been the team that says 'this is broken' out loud, and that's not changing. Ask questions, flag blockers, and please keep speculation about the acquisition in the #watercooler thread, not in work channels.

communities.notes: About 25 testers in Montréal. Used to be a flat, informal studio where QA could talk directly to designers. Now new managers, processes and reporting lines from the parent company are arriving, and people are anxious about layoffs.

communities.name: Philippine Nurses Abroad Network

description.purpose: For Filipino nurses working or planning to work abroad: NCLEX, licensing, visas, agencies and job tips.
description.culture: No agency spam.

communities.notes: About 40,000 members across the US, UK, Middle East and Australia. Run by a few admins who are themselves nurses abroad, with frequent fights over recruitment agencies posting in disguise.

communities.name: P4 Blue Parents

description.purpose: For parents and guardians of P4 Blue at Kampala Junior Academy. Teacher Grace posts homework, test dates, and reminders about school events. Parents can ask questions about class matters and share information.
description.culture: Kindly keep messages to class matters. Fees questions go to the bursar's office, not this group. Address the teacher respectfully and give her time to respond outside school hours. No forwards, no politics.

communities.notes: About 40 parents and the class teacher, who is the only admin. A few parents use the group to complain about teaching publicly, and the teacher has considered making it admin-only posting.

communities.name: Tenants in Struggle Lisbon

description.purpose:
We are tenants in Lisbon fighting evictions, illegal rent increases and the conversion of our homes into tourist flats. We help each other: we go to court with neighbours, show up when the bailiffs come, pressure landlords, share legal knowledge, and organise demonstrations for the right to housing. About 1,000 of us are in the Signal groups, and we meet in neighbourhood assemblies in Mouraria, Penha de França, Arroios and Marvila.

We have no leaders, no president and no board. On purpose. We've seen too many movements captured by a few voices, co-opted by parties, or broken when the leader burned out or was targeted. So:

- Decisions are made in assemblies. Each neighbourhood assembly meets weekly. A general assembly of all neighbourhoods meets monthly. Anyone affected can come and speak.
- We decide by consensus where we can. If we can't reach consensus after two meetings, we vote, with two-thirds needed.
- Spokespeople rotate. Whoever talks to journalists or the city council is chosen for that specific occasion by the assembly, and nobody can be a spokesperson twice in a row. They speak for the assembly's decision, not their own opinion.
- Tasks are done by working groups (legal, communications, eviction response, welcome), which anyone can join. Working groups report to the assembly.
- Nobody is paid, and we don't accept money from political parties.

The Signal groups: one announcement group (only working groups post), one per neighbourhood, and one emergency group for eviction alerts. Please don't use the emergency group for anything else.

What's hard right now: a TV station wanted 'the leader of the movement' for a debate and wouldn't accept a rotating spokesperson. Some members think we lost a big opportunity; others think saying yes would have created exactly the kind of leader we don't want. Also, the communications working group has been the same four people for a year, because nobody else joins, and that's making people uneasy.
description.culture: Solidarity, not charity. You don't need to be an activist to be here; you just need to live somewhere. Speak in Portuguese, English, Creole, Bengali, whatever you need, and we'll find someone to translate.

communities.notes: Deliberately leaderless and assembly-run, which protects it from capture but makes it slow and invisible to media. In practice, the few people who do the most work have informal influence the structure was designed to prevent.

communities.name: Sunday Kite Flyers Karachi

description.purpose: Kite lovers of Karachi! We meet on Sunday mornings at Sea View or the open ground in Clifton (location posted Saturday night) to fly kites, have fights, and drink chai. Tips on making and repairing kites, and where to buy good ones.
description.culture: Safety first: NO metal or glass-coated string, ever. People have died. No flying near power lines. Everyone shares their spool with the kids.

communities.notes: About 90 members, mostly men from different ages and neighbourhoods. The safety rule is the one thing enforced strictly; the group admin will remove anyone who brags about using coated string.

communities.name: PolyDict

description.purpose: Free, collaborative dictionaries for languages the big dictionaries forgot.

communities.notes: About 2,000 editors across roughly 80 language editions, each with its own small community and reviewer team. Native speakers and outside linguists sometimes disagree sharply about who gets to decide what's correct.

communities.name: Interfaith Sunday Hikers

description.purpose: Every other Sunday afternoon we hike in the Front Range with people of different faiths and none. Each hike includes a short pause where someone shares a reading, prayer, poem or reflection from their tradition, followed by conversation on the trail. Hikes are moderate and family-friendly.
description.culture: Curiosity over conversion. Listen more than you talk, and nobody has to share. Leave no trace, and bring enough water.

communities.notes: About 150 members on Meetup, organised by a rabbi, a Lutheran pastor and a Muslim chaplain. Half come for the dialogue and half for the hikes, and the organisers disagree about whether to add harder hikes that would draw more hikers but fewer families.
communities.setupNotes: could be hobby; Meetup doesn't fit formats well

communities.name: Marine Acoustics Group

description.purpose:
This is the workspace for the Marine Acoustics Group at the university in Tromsø. We study the Arctic underwater soundscape: whale and seal vocalisations, ice noise, and the effects of shipping and seismic surveys on marine mammals. We have long-term hydrophone moorings in the Barents Sea and around Svalbard, and we run two to three cruises a year.

How we use Slack and the mailing list:
- #general for group news. The mailing list is for official things (cruise announcements, deadlines, seminars) so that collaborators outside the group get them too.
- #fieldwork for cruise planning and mooring logistics. Sign up for cruises using the form pinned there.
- #data for questions about the acoustic archive, processing pipelines and annotation tools.
- #papers-and-drafts for sharing drafts and asking for internal review.
- #random for everything else, including the coffee machine situation.

Some group agreements, discussed and updated at our yearly retreat:

Data: All raw recordings go to the group archive within a month of recovery, with metadata following the template. Data from the moorings is shared across the group; you don't 'own' a mooring. If you want to use data that someone else is actively working on, talk to them first.

Authorship: We use contribution-based authorship. Whoever leads the analysis and writing is first author. Anyone who did significant fieldwork, data processing or analysis for that paper is offered co-authorship. The person who deployed and recovered the moorings is offered authorship on the first two papers from that dataset. Disagreements go to Ingrid (PI), but please try to settle them yourselves first.

Fieldwork: Cruise spots are limited. Priority goes to people whose projects need that cruise, then to people who haven't been at sea recently. Everyone does the HSE course before their first cruise. Nobody is ever pressured to go to sea, and nobody is penalised for saying no.

Working hours: We work with people in many time zones, but please don't expect replies on evenings and weekends, except during cruises.
description.culture: We're a friendly, fairly informal group. Ask questions early, especially if you're new to acoustics. Credit people generously.

communities.notes: About 18 people: PI, two researchers, postdocs, PhD students, an engineer, plus visiting collaborators. The written agreements are good, but the PI still effectively decides cruise places, and postdocs worry about whose name goes on the mooring papers.

communities.name: Mosquito Watch Senegal

description.purpose: Volunteers in Dakar, Thiès and Saint-Louis help track where mosquitoes are breeding. Take a photo of standing water or larvae with the app, and it goes on a map shared with health teams and researchers. The WhatsApp group is for questions, training sessions, and updates on what the data shows.
description.culture: Everyone can help, even with an old phone. Only post photos you took yourself. No medical advice in the group: if someone is sick, they go to the health post.

communities.notes: About 1,200 volunteers, many recruited through schools and women's groups. Run by a research institute with a community coordinator in each city; volunteers complain that they rarely hear what happens after they report a site.

communities.name: Lounge 42

description.purpose: Talk about anything.
